lines.text: Why do phone manufacturers suddenly stop sending software updates to perfectly working older phones?
It is not just a greedy plan to force you to buy a new device.
The real bottleneck is the chipset manufacturer who built the processor inside your phone.
Companies like Qualcomm only support driver patches for their microchips for four to five years.
Newer operating systems require modern neural engines, larger RAM, and advanced GPU instruction sets.
Without chipmaker driver support, installing new updates would cause phones to lag, overheat, and crash.
Once updates stop, unpatched security vulnerabilities make it time for a phone upgrade.
